title: Deployment-stage execution
summary: Materialization reuses schema metadata and one operation-local run/stage membership read; plan groups read live attachments and fresh withdrawals. Admission and source/target authority remain checked by their existing owners. Production proof resolves the member project explicitly and checks public-ref wire identity; missions record actual population and retain the relay deadline. Execution-count observations match the exact run, stage and member, excluding concurrent campaigns for unrelated subjects. Takeover changes current run ownership in existing records; snapshots, requirement IDs, execution IDs, cursor, leases, review bundles and prior observations remain intact. Successor materialization reuses inherited item-case, open plan-group and run-level rows and adds genuinely new obligations; closed plan groups stay in the run where they passed. Execution-ID continuation is available while the successor is created, deploying or failed, without granting stage acceptance. An inherited FAIL is retried as a fresh attempt on the same requirement; when the successor's release contains the item's merge, its owner gets one retry handoff, even if that owner produced the FAIL. Deployment QA stages select cases for their declared target environment; choosing a flow and its targets carries execution mechanics without enforcing release order or requiring a production-role target.
